summary: Hostname suffix truncation during imaging causes Intune device object merge and check-in flapping
description:
Issue summary: Devices imaged with the new OEM task sequence (ts-2026-03) are being assigned hostnames that get truncated by a legacy hostname-sanitize script to 15 characters. When the corporate DNS suffix is later appended by the join script the resulting FQDN collides with an existing device name in Intune/Azure AD. Intune merges device objects in some cases when the primary DNS/hostname matches, causing device check-in to alternate between two device objects (flapping) and blocking configuration profiles/policy assignment.

Impact: Multiple newly imaged seats in prod-us-west and APAC are failing to receive critical configuration profiles; desktop management and endpoint security policies not applied. Affected users report intermittent policy loss and inability to access mapped network printers. No data loss reported, but this blocks autopilot/dedicated device rollouts and delays repairs.

Observed behavior: Hostnames generated by ts-2026-03 look correct during imaging (example: rw-infer-nyc-emb-20260312), but after the legacy sanitize step the local .computername gets truncated to 15 chars (rw-infer-nyc-eb). When domain join/appending-suffix runs we end up with rw-infer-nyc-eb.corp.redwood.com which matches an existing old device object (previously registered) and Azure AD/Intune merges or links to the older object. This creates two Azure device IDs with the same physical machine reporting intermittently and both show check-ins.

Expected behavior: Hostname sanitization should preserve uniqueness used by TS naming templates or the join process should ensure a stable, unique device identifier is used for Intune registration (preferably HW hash/autopilot entry), avoiding collisions with legacy objects.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use imaging task sequence ts-2026-03 that runs hostname template: rw-infer-<region>-<team>-<shortdate>.
2) Run legacy hostname sanitize script (hostname-sanitize.sh) which truncates to first 15 characters for legacy NetBIOS compatibility.
3) Complete OOBE and domain join which appends corporate suffix.
4) Observe Intune portal: device appears to merge with an existing device object which has matching shortname; check-in timestamps alternate between two device IDs.
5) Reproducible on repro VM/hardware with imported autopilot hardware hash for same model.

Notes: Repro only after the sanitize step is executed; skipping sanitize prevents the merge.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: hostname truncate to 15 chars causes name collisions with older device records created prior to autopilot rollouts. Verified by imaging a test unit and checking AAD device list - old device (decommissioned) reused same shortname.
What we tried:
- Re-imaging and excluding sanitize script -> new device registers cleanly (no merge).
- Created synthetic long hostnames and observed Azure registers new device id consistently.
- Queried AAD for duplicates: ran Powershell 'Get-AzureADDevice -Filter "startswith(displayName,'rw-infer-nyc')"' and found 3 objects with same shortname lowercased causing merge logic to trigger.
- Cross-checked with #internal-provisioning Slack thread and found a recent deploy of hostname-sanitize.sh with change that enforces NetBIOS only; likely merged in January image baseline (ref: git commit abc123 in infra-images).

Root cause candidate: combination of (a) legacy sanitize step truncating NetBIOS name to 15 chars, (b) autopilot/device enrollment behavior that sometimes links by hostname when HW hash is missing or duplicate, and (c) leftover old AAD device objects that match truncated names.

Telemetry/metrics: 8 devices reported in last 48h with merge behavior; 5 currently in 'check-in flapping' state.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:15 - Asha Ray (reporter): Uploaded logs and repro steps. Noted that this started after ts-2026-03 rollout last week.

2026-03-12 13:03 - Miguel Torres (assignee): Confirmed repro on bench hardware. Skipped sanitize step and enrollment succeeded. Marking sanitize script as likely cause. Will coordinate hotfix to imaging TS.

2026-03-13 09:22 - Priya Patel (SRE): Observed related AAD device cleanup backlog in us-west; recommended we run bulk soft-delete of stale device objects that match naming pattern after we confirm fix to avoid accidental removals. Added to follow-up playbook.

2026-03-14 08:48 - Miguel Torres: Rolling a temporary mitigation: patched ts-2026-03 to skip hostname-sanitize step and added a post-image policy to validate uniqueness before domain join. Pushing to 50 pilot seats in prod-us-west.
resolution: Workaround: Patched ts-2026-03 to skip legacy hostname-sanitize; added pre-join uniqueness check (script verifies no existing AAD objects with same shortname). For devices already merged: manual remediation steps documented (rename device in Intune OR retire old object and re-enroll). Permanent fix: update image pipeline to remove NetBIOS truncation and add autopilot hardware-hash validation prior to AAD join. Follow-up action: schedule AAD device cleanup run subject to coordination with SRE and inventory team. Target for full rollout: 2026-03-20.
